title: Operational budgets and native XTP pacing
summary: Memory Fabric candidate2 uses OperationalCapacityGovernor dev5 to acquire/reconcile real admission tickets and XTP dev25 capacityRate to enforce live per-context rate on named-service control sends.
invariants: A 64 MiB aligned block window may be split across two independently authorised resident suppliers; each 30% with max parallel 2 and aggregate 60% is an example policy, not a fixed fabric default.
Aggregate percent constrains the number of full-share contexts: floor(aggregate/perContext) bounds fan-in before tickets are acquired.
The operational class is registered locally, not accepted from a sender header; ingress capacity domain accounting is in the receiver/placement administrative domain.
Rate is derived from the current capacity ticket. A socket without CAPACITYRATE is refused rather than downgraded to an unlimited sender.
At zero effective capacity, emergency suspension, expired ticket, stale owner epoch, or absent replica-authority proof: no send.
Live proof covers named-service bounded control payload over loopback UDP (300,000 then 150,000 bytes/s). It is NOT a verified multi-MU memory-page transfer or multicast discovery proof.

provenance.claim: Capacity registry, shared governor, refresh and reconcile tickets.
